items.title: Opportunities and risks of big data for the methods and culture of psychological science
items.author: Jessica L. Tracy
items.content: Big data can address problems with generalizability and enable the study of real-world behaviours. However, the overuse of big data could lead to over-reliance on correlations bereft of explanatory power. In this Perspective, Ibasco et al. describe the methodological and cultural opportunities and risks of big data for psychological science.

items.title: Prediction in language comprehension across the lifespan
items.author: Yukun Yu
items.content: Comprehending language involves active prediction of what might occur next. In this Review, Federmeier and colleagues synthesize evidence from children, young adults and older adults to show how prediction is dynamically engaged for language comprehension across the lifespan.

items.title: The role of hippocampus-based developmental changes in paediatric post-traumatic stress disorder
items.author: Dylan G. Gee
items.content: The treatment of paediatric post-traumatic stress disorder currently focuses on associative processes that have primarily been studied in adults. In this Perspective, Foster et al. spotlight higher-order learning processes that typically develop during childhood to specify intervention targets for young patients.
